I'm weighing the first candidate, "autosomal recessive familial neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus," as a Specific Disease, since it is the most specific form and the full string is the minimum necessary span.

I'm now going through the second candidate, "familial neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus," which I'm treating as a Specific Disease since it names one particular condition. For the third, "autosomal dominant disorder," I'm weighing whether it counts as a Disease Class, given the guideline example that treats "autosomal recessive disease" that way, even though "disorder" on its own would be a general term.

I'm checking whether "arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency" counts as a disease, since it is the biochemical cause of central diabetes insipidus. The guideline excludes "deficiency" as a general term on its own, but a specific deficiency like "C7 deficiency" is treated as a Specific Disease, so this one might be too.

I'm leaning toward calling "arginine vasopressin deficiency" a Specific Disease, since it names a particular condition much like "C7 deficiency" does. The "deficiency of active AVP" mention is more of a general description, so I'm weighing whether it should be left out.

I'm still weighing whether "arginine vasopressin deficiency" and "deficiency of active AVP" should both be annotated, since they describe the same underlying condition. Treating the first as a specific disease while leaving the second out would be inconsistent, so I'm considering marking both the same way, or neither.

I'm settling on SpecificDisease for "arginine vasopressin deficiency," since it names a particular condition the way "C7 deficiency" does. I'm leaning toward NONE for the "deficiency of active AVP" mention, because there it reads as a generic physiological description rather than a named disease.

I'm now settling on neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus as a Specific Disease, since it's named again in a separate sentence about three affected children, and repeat mentions like that are annotated each time.

I'm settling on NONE for "deficiency of active AVP," since "deficiency" alone is a general term and this phrase describes a generic physiological state in a hypothetical context rather than naming a disease; the disease itself is already captured by the "AVP deficiency" mention.

I'm settling on SpecificDisease for "arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency," since it's an explicit condition named in the disease description. I'll keep that label.
